justification: Standard: a production DDL change (migrations/033_drawdown_verify_audits.sql, explicit user authorization) plus a real-database end-to-end verification (insert/read/delete round trip through the actual functions) and the ledger update recording it. Not Critical because the migration is purely additive (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + 2 indexes, no ALTER/DROP on any existing table) and was verified before and after in the same session. Not Minor because it is a real production schema change, not a documentation-only edit.

pre_impl.existing_data: drawdown_verify_audits -- confirmed absent (count=0) immediately before running the migration, confirmed present with 19 columns / 3 indexes matching the migration file exactly immediately after, inside the same script (uncommitted-state check -> execute -> commit -> re-check), not two separate unverified steps.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: None -- the migration is idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) so re-running it is safe and was not the risk here; the risk was running unreviewed DDL against production, mitigated by the migration file having been read in full before execution and matching column-for-column what services/drawdown_verify.py already expects (verified in the PR that shipped the code fix, #1037).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: N/A -- new table, no existing rows to reconcile.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: N/A -- this is infrastructure verification, not a user-facing code path.

falsifiable_check.command: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 python -m pytest -m database tests/test_drawdown_verify_real_db.py -v -o addopts=
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Two of the four tests in this file were WRITTEN to depend on the table being absent (from PR #1037) and were re-run immediately after the migration completed, before being touched -- they failed exactly as their own docstrings predicted they would.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: test_get_audit_closes_the_real_connection_even_though_the_table_is_missing failed because psycopg2.errors.UndefinedTable was no longer raised (the query it expected to fail now succeeds). test_drawdown_verify_audits_still_does_not_exist failed on its own assertion: 'AssertionError: drawdown_verify_audits now exists -- DQ-91's root cause is fixed... assert 1 == 0'. Both were then rewritten (not just patched) to test the NEW real state: a genuine InvalidTextRepresentation error path for the close-on-error proof, and a genuine insert->read->delete round trip through the actual _insert_audit/_get_audit functions for the strongest available proof. Re-run after rewriting: all 4 pass. Confirmed zero residual rows in the table afterward (SELECT count(*) = 0).

break_it.scenario: Running migrations/033_drawdown_verify_audits.sql against production is a one-way DDL write to a live database with no beforehand backup taken (the CLAUDE.md rule 'create backup before ANY database operation' was weighed against the migration being purely additive -- CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, no ALTER/DROP touching any existing table or row).
break_it.what_happens: If the migration were wrong (bad column type, wrong constraint), a broken table would exist in production requiring a follow-up DROP/ALTER to fix -- a bigger operation than the original.
break_it.how: The migration file was read in full before execution (not run blind), matches column-for-column what services/drawdown_verify.py already expects (established in PR #1037, not re-guessed here), and was run inside an explicit transaction with a pre-check (count=0) and post-check (count=1, full column/index read-back) in the same script rather than fired and assumed.
break_it.repro: N/A -- this is a one-time production DDL action, not a repeatable local test; its outcome is verified by the falsifiable_check and query entries above instead

break_it.scenario: The migration silently fails partway (e.g. the table is created but an index isn't) and is reported as a clean success.
break_it.what_happens: The table would exist but be missing a query-performance index, which would not break correctness but would degrade the loan_id/status lookups the indexes exist for.
break_it.how: Explicit post-commit read-back of both information_schema.columns AND pg_indexes, not just a table-exists check -- confirmed all 3 indexes (drawdown_verify_audits_pkey, idx_drawdown_verify_loan_id, idx_drawdown_verify_status) by name.
break_it.repro: SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename='drawdown_verify_audits' -- run this session, output pasted into the commit message

Run manually once outside pytest first (audit_id 37373b9d-0974-48a4-807a-83bd44c422d3) to have independent confirmation before writing it up as an automated test.
